b.e43effd6e3:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>P</c>ange, lingua, gloriósi
Prœlium certáminis,
Et super Crucis trophǽo
Dic triúmphum nóbilem,
Quáliter Redémptor orbis
Immolátus vícerit.

<h>D</h>e paréntis protoplásti
Fraude Factor cóndolens,
Quando pomi noxiális
Morsu in mortem córruit,
Ipse lignum tunc notávit,
Damna ligni ut sólveret.

<h>H</h>oc opus nostræ salútis
Ordo depopóscerat,
Multifórmis proditóris
Ars ut artem fálleret,
Et medélam ferret inde,
Hostis unde lǽserat.

<h>Q</h>uando venit ergo sacri
Plenitúdo témporis,
Missus est ab arce Patris
Natus, orbis Cónditor,
Atque ventre virgináli
Carne amíctus pródiit.

<h>V</h>agit infans inter arcta
Cónditus præsépia:
Membra pannis involúta
Virgo Mater álligat:
Et manus, pedésque, et crura
Stricta cingit fáscia.

<h>G</h>lória, et honor Deo
Usqueqáque Altíssimo,
Una Patri, Filióque;
Inclyto Paráclito:
Cui laus est et potéstas,
Per ætérna sǽcula.
Amen.
b.a8f191c38e:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>S</c>ing, my tongue, the glorious battle
Sing the last, the dread affray;
O'er the cross, the victor's trophy,
Sound the high triumphal lay:
Tell how Christ, the world's Redeemer,
As a victim won the day.

<h>G</h>od, his Maker, sorely grieving
That the first-made Adam fell,
When he ate the fruit of sorrow,
Whose reward was death and hell,
Noted then this wood, the ruin
Of the ancient wood to quell.

<h>F</h>or the work of our salvation
Needs would have his order so,
And the multiform deceiver's
Art by art would overthrow,
And from thence would bring the med'cine
Whence the insult of the foe.

<h>W</h>herefore, when the sacred fullness
Of the appointed time was come,
This world's Maker left his Father,
Sent the heav'nly mansion from,
And proceeded, God Incarnate,
Of the Virgin's holy womb.

<h>W</h>eeps the infant in the manger
That in Bethlehem's stable stands;
And his limbs the Virgin Mother
Doth compose in swaddling bands,
Meetly thus in linen folding
Of her God the feet and hands.

<h>T</h>o the Trinity be glory
Everlasting, as is meet;
Equal to the Father, equal
To the Son, and Paraclete:
Trinal Unity, whose praises
All created things repeat.
Amen.

<c>L</c>ustris sex qui jam peráctis,
Tempus implens córporis,
Se volénte natus ad hoc,
Passióni déditus,
Agnus in Crucis levátur
Immolándus stípite.

<h>H</h>ic acétum, fel, arúndo,
Sputa, clavi, láncea:
Mite corpus perforátur,
Sanguis, unda prófluit:
Terra, pontus, astra, mundus,
Quo lavántur flúmine!

<h>C</h>rux fidélis, inter omnes
Arbor una nóbilis:
Nulla silva talem profert
Fronde, flore, gérmine:
Dulce lignum, dulces clavos,
Dulce pondus sústinet.

<h>F</h>lecte ramos, arbor alta,
Tensa laxa víscera,
Et rigor lentéscat ille,
Quem dedit natívitas:
Ut supérni membra Regis
Miti tendas stípite.

<h>S</h>ola digna tu fuísti
Ferre sæcli prétium,
Atque portum præparáre
Nauta mundo náufrago,
Quem sacer cruor perúnxit,
Fusus Agni córpore.

<h>G</h>lória et honor Deo
Usquequáque altíssimo:
Una Patri, Filióque,
Inclyto Paráclito:
Cui laus est et potéstas
Per ætérna sǽcula.

<c>T</c>hirty years among us dwelling,
His appointed time fulfilled,
Born for this, he meets his passion,
For that this he freely willed:
On the cross the Lamb is lifted,
Where his life-blood shall be spilled.

<h>H</h>e endured the nails, the spitting,
Vinegar, and spear, and reed;
From that holy body broken
Blood and water forth proceed:
Earth, and stars, and sky, and ocean,
By that flood from stain are free.

<h>F</h>aithful cross! above all other,
One and only noble tree!
None in foliage, none in blossom,
None in fruit thy peers may be;
Sweetest wood and sweetest iron!
Sweetest weight is hung on thee.

<h>B</h>end thy boughs, O tree of glory!
Thy relaxing sinews bend;
For awhile the ancient rigour,
That thy birth bestowed, suspend;
And the King of heavenly beauty
On thy bosom gently tend!

<h>T</h>hou alone wast counted worthy
This world's ransom to uphold;
For a shipwrecked race preparing
Harbour, like the ark of old;
With the sacred blood anointed
From the smitten Lamb that rolled.

<h>T</h>o the Trinity be glory
Everlasting, as is meet;
Equal to the Father, equal
To the Son, and Paraclete:
Trinal Unity, whose praises
All created things repeat.
Amen.

b.7fba191d19:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>M</c>arch 24th 2027, the 16th day of the Moon,
<h>O</h>n the morrow we keep the feast of the holy Archangel Gabriel, who announced to the Blessed Virgin Mary the mystery of the Incarnation of the Lord.
<h>U</h>pon the same 24th day of March, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy martyr Epigmenius, a Priest, who was slain with the sword, by order of the judge Turpius, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.
<h>L</h>ikewise at Rome, the blessed martyr Pigmenius, a Priest, who was cast into the river Tiber for Christ's faith's sake, under the Emperor Julian the Apostate.
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy martyrs Mark and Timothy, who were crowned with martyrdom under the Emperor Antonine.
<h>A</h>t Caesarea, in Palestine, were born into the better life: the holy martyrs Timolaus, Denis, Pausides, Romulus, Alexander, another Alexander, Agapius, and another Denis, who won crowns of life by the axe, under the president Urban, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.
<h>I</h>n Morocco, were born into the better life: the holy brethren Romulus and Secundus, both martyrs, who suffered for Christ's faith, [in the year 304.]
<h>A</h>t Trent, the holy child Simeon, most cruelly murdered by the Jews, and who afterwards shone with many miracles, [in the year 1475.]
<h>A</h>t Synnada, in Phrygia, holy Agapitus, Bishop of that see, [under Maximin 234-238.]
<h>A</h>t Brescia, holy Latinus, Bishop of that see, [beginning of second century.]
<h>I</h>n Syria, the holy Confessor Seleucus.
<h>I</h>n Sweden, the holy Virgin Katherine, daughter of holy Bridget, [in the year 1381.]
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

Hoc Passiónis témpore
Auge piis justítiam,
Reísque dona véniam.

<h>T</h>e summa, Deus, Trínitas,
Colláudet omnis spíritus:
Quos per Crucis mystérium
Salvas, rege per sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Éripe me, Dómine, ab hómine malo.
<r>℟.</r> A viro iníquo éripe me.
b.898e829c01:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Jer 11:20</r>
<c>B</c>ut thou, O Lord of Sabaoth, who judgest justly, and triest the reins and hearts, let me see thy revenge on them: for to thee I have revealed my cause, O Lord my God.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>A</c>broad the regal banners fly,
Now shines the cross’s mystery;
Upon it Life did death endure,
And yet by death did life procure.

<h>W</h>ho, wounded with a direful spear,
Did, purposely to wash us clear
From stain of sin, pour out a flood
Of precious water mixed with blood.

<h>T</h>hat which the prophet-king of old
Hath in mysterious verse foretold,
Is now accomplished, whilst we see
God ruling nations from a tree.

<h>O</h> lovely and refulgent tree,
Adorned with purpled majesty;
Culled from a worthy stock, to bear
Those limbs which sanctifièd were.

<h>B</h>lest tree, whose happy branches bore
The wealth that did the world restore;
The beam that did that body weigh
Which raised up hell’s expected prey.

<r>The following verse is said on bended knee.</r>

<h>O</h> Cross, our one reliance, hail!
This holy Passiontide avail
To give fresh merit to the saint,
And pardon to the penitent.

<h>B</h>lest Trinity, salvation’s spring,
May every soul thy praises sing;
To those thou grantest conquest by
The holy cross, rewards apply.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man.
<r>℟.</r> Rescue me from the unjust man.

b.f1ea880604:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>T</c>ua nos misericórdia, Deus, et ab omni subreptióne vetustátis expúrget: et capáces sanctæ novitátis effíciat.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.086f7a7055:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>M</c>ay thy mercy, O God, cleanse us from the deceits of our old nature, and enable us to be formed anew unto holiness.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Ant.</r> O Rex glorióse inter Sanctos tuos, qui semper es laudábilis et tamen ineffábilis: tu in nobis es, Dómine, et nomen sanctum tuum invocátum est super nos: ne derelínquas nos Deus noster: ut in die judícii nos collocáre dignéris inter Sanctos et Eléctos tuos, Rex benedícte.

<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>O</c>mnípotens sempitérne Deus: da nobis ita Domínicæ passiónis sacraménta perágere; ut indulgéntiam percípere mereámur.
<h>P</h>er eúndem Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum Fílium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.

<h>T</h>hrough the same Jesus Christ, thy Son, Our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
